label: copy phase, from 4th output on (not last), input token in {n,g,p,f,z,r,s,j,i,o}
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase: never on original-token steps, never at the delimiter, and almost never on the first three copy outputs (recall_idx 0-1 essentially zero, 2 weak). It is active only where the fed-back input token is a repeat (in_first=0, which follows from the copy phase). Most mass falls at recall_idx 3-4 (about 75%), with a smaller rise at recall_idx 7-8 in long sequences. It is weak on the final output step and gets more frequent with longer L (L<=4 never). Within that window, the identity of the fed-back input token modulates firing strongly: n, g, p, f and z have rates 2.5-3.7x the base rate, r, s and j are moderate, and o, u and b are low. The strongest activations are at recall_idx 3 with input g, n, p or f (input = orig(2)). The output token adds a weaker effect (v, i, h, u and s outputs are elevated). Position alone (recall_idx>=3, not last) gives recall 0.87 but precision 0.23. Adding the token set gives F1 about 0.53 on dev. The token preference is graded rather than a clean set, so precision and recall both stay incomplete.
